# 0.3.4 routing research (2026-11-13 UTC)

## Evidence and limits

- [Priors Terminal-Bench v4-AA](https://www.mypriors.com/benchmarks/aa-terminalbench-v4-0), data as of 2026-11-12, 66 technical tasks, three runs, mini-SWE-agent: Kimi K3.1 max 67.2%, listed $5.27/task; GPT-6.1 Terra max 55.6%, $0.057/task; GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh 54.0%, $0.034/task. The site says cost is median subscription estimate, **or API price if no plan data**. Kimi's $5.27 equals its API figure; the row does not establish a subscription estimate. These are published harness estimates, not local measurements; max is outside the requested Terra low–xhigh range.
- [Priors Luna model](https://www.mypriors.com/models/gpt-6-luna): Terminal-Bench v4 medium 2.5%, high 4.5%; this is not a review benchmark and does not establish reviewer quality or per-effort subscription cost. [Priors FrontierCode 2.0](https://www.mypriors.com/benchmarks/bg-frontier-code-v2), data 2026-11-12, reports Luna max 21.9%, Kimi K3.1 max 19.6%; evaluates change generation, not code review. Neither source supports medium-versus-high review ranking.
- The Kimi extension's [upstream README](https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code) documents opt-in `moonshot_search` and `moonshot_fetch`, requiring OAuth and eligible account; API key alone is insufficient. [Moonshot's Kimi CLI docs](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli/blob/main/docs/en/configuration/providers.md) independently describe Kimi Code search/fetch as services unavailable when unconfigured. This does not prove host/account availability or cross-model invocation. Upstream main may differ from locked pi-provider-kimi-code 0.6.13.
- [OpenAI web-search docs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search) establish Responses API capability, not a callable tool in this Pi Codex adapter. Actual Codex native web tool exposure remains unknown; registry or generic API presence is insufficient.
- Repo: `packages/runtime/src/pi/provider.ts:93-115` uses one selected profile for all rows; `:176-184` searches only that profile and chooses web-kit if empty. Thus Codex selected + installed Kimi means Kimi is never consulted. `:56-74` names Kimi tools and no Codex tools; `setup/pi-settings.ts:53-54` notes locked Kimi tools default off. `config/schema.ts:66-115` uses Kimi for Coding aliases, whose model identity can change, and `pi/codex/routes.ts` supplies Sol/Terra/Luna and effort defaults. Actual alias mapping/account entitlement is unverified. Strict structured-output support remains unknown for each endpoint except prior task history's bounded Luna medium guardian-schema example, not general certification.

## Implementable scoring and routing boundary

Import versioned, dated evidence for each provider/model/effort/task benchmark, harness, exact subscription plan, per-task effective subscription cost and provenance; reject API-price fallbacks. Resolve mutable aliases from account catalog without treating that as capability proof. Apply hard role/capability filters (screen input, tools, output schema, permissions, provider availability); unknown is ineligible for a required capability. For comparable same-benchmark rows with strictly positive subscription cost, define value `quality / cost` and score `value / max(value of eligible comparable rows)`, yielding [0,1]. Declare dataset, confidence and assumptions; avoid mixing benchmarks or averaging unsupported effort values. Set score unknown, not zero, for missing/stale data or unavailable account, with a documented freshness policy and an explicit pinned safe configured fallback. Do not claim an optimized winner until comparable rows cover each candidate and role.

Support independent provider per role and preserve user-selected root/defaults. Concrete interim configuration: Codex Terra medium–xhigh for assigned specialists per current user selection; enable Kimi as a configurable independent route for validated compatible non-screen work when explicitly selected, without representing it as a measured winner. After evidence import select the highest score among role-eligible candidates; if insufficient, surface unresolved ranking. Luna medium/high review needs matching reviewer benchmark and subscription costs. The product requirement for evidence-backed mixed routing remains open.

For provider-first web, inventory all installed extensions and their actually exposed, enabled and authorized search/fetch tools independently of current model; choose a supported installed native adapter first, respecting off/explicit overrides, session permissions and account limits. Unknown or disabled capability is distinct from confirmed absent; surface diagnostics and never treat a transient auth/network failure as proof of absence. Verify whether a Kimi tool can execute while the active model is Codex before choosing it. Only after no installed provider offers callable search, select an explicitly configured web-kit/Exa fallback, with missing-key error surfaced; identify public search available in the host separately, not as a guaranteed Pi integration. Preserve current guardrails and avoid silent credential/config changes.
